questions.text:
Each of a set of n processes executes the following code using two semaphores a and b initialized to 1 and 0, respectively. Assume that count is a shared variable initialized to 0 and not used in CODE SECTION P.

What does the code achieve?
questions.solution:
Semaphore a protects count; b starts at 0.
- Each process increments count after CODE SECTION P, then waits on b.
- Only the n-th (last) process signals b; then each process that passes wait(b) signals b again for the next one.

So nobody enters CODE SECTION Q until all n processes have finished P. This is a barrier.

Answer: No process executes CODE SECTION Q before every process has finished CODE SECTION P

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: It ensures that no process executes CODE SECTION Q before every process has finished CODE SECTION P.
It ensures that two processes are in CODE SECTION Q at any time.
It ensures that all processes execute CODE SECTION P mutually exclusively.
It ensures that at most n-1 processes are in CODE SECTION P at any time.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about process state transitions for a system using preemptive scheduling.

I. A running process can move to ready state.
II. A ready process can move to running state.
III. A blocked process can move to running state.
IV. A blocked process can move to ready state.

Which of the above statements are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Running [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Ready (preemption) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] possible.
- Ready [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Running (dispatch) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] possible.
- Blocked [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Running [latex]\text{---}[/latex] not possible; a blocked process goes to Ready first.
- Blocked [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Ready (I/O done) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] possible.

Answer: I, II and IV only

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: I, II, III and IV only

questions.text: Consider allocation of memory to a new process. Assume that none of the existing holes in the memory will exactly fit the process's memory requirement. Hence, a new hole of smaller size will be created if allocation is made in any of the existing holes. Which one of the following statement is TRUE?
questions.solution:
Best fit picks the smallest hole that fits, so the hole it leaves is the smallest possible. First fit picks some fitting hole, so its leftover is never smaller than best fit's.

The other comparisons depend on where the holes are and are not "always" true.

Answer: The hole created by best fit is never larger than the hole created by first fit

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: The hole created by first fit is always larger than the hole created by next fit.
The hole created by worst fit is always larger than the hole created by first fit.
The hole created by best fit is never larger than the hole created by first fit.
The hole created by next fit is never larger than the hole created by best fit.

questions.text: The index node (inode) of a Unix-like file system has 12 direct, one single-indirect and one double-indirect pointer The disk block size is 4 kB and the disk block addresses 32-bits long. The maximum possible file size is (rounded off to 1 decimal place) __________ GB.
questions.solution:
Pointers per block = 4 KB / 4 B = 1024.
- Direct: 12 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 KB = 48 KB
- Single indirect: 1024 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 KB = 4 MB
- Double indirect: [latex]1024^2[/latex] [latex]\times[/latex] 4 KB = 4 GB

Total [latex]\approx[/latex] 4 GB + 4 MB + 48 KB [latex]\approx[/latex] 4.0 GB

Answer: 4.0

questions.text:
Consider the following four processes with arrival times (in milliseconds) and their length of CPU burst (in milliseconds) as shown below:
These processes are run on a single processor using preemptive Shortest Remaining Time First scheduling algorithm. If the average waiting time of the processes is 1 millisecond, then the value of Z is __________.
questions.solution:
Average waiting time 1 ms [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] total waiting time = 4 ms.

SRTF up to t = 4: P1 runs 0-1; P2 (burst 1) preempts and runs 1-2; P1 runs 2-4 and finishes. P1 waited 1, P2 waited 0.

At t = 4, P3 (3 ms, arrived at 3) and P4 (Z) are left. For the total to be 4, they must wait 3 in total.
With Z = 2: P4 runs 4-6 (wait 0), P3 runs 6-9 (wait 9 [latex]-[/latex] 3 [latex]-[/latex] 3 = 3). Total = 1 + 0 + 3 + 0 = 4 True

Answer: 2
